evidence.ref: A versioned decision-review artifact format (schema warp.decision_review/v1) is homed per-repo under .warp/decision_reviews/*.yaml, a directory the engine glob (.warp/*.yaml is non-recursive) does not sweep, so reviews stay per-repo like the decision records and are never shipped in the engine. A review binds to a decision (decision id + decision_version) and captures the attack on the framing: a problem_class challenge, a non-empty option_challenges list (each judging whether an option's dead_end holds), a missing_options list, a non-empty assumption_challenges list (each judging whether an assumption is load-bearing), a recommendation, and a disposition. The illustrative example ships at .warp/examples/decision-review-example.yaml reviewing the shipped decision-example (DEC-0000) in its draft state. python3 .warp/validate.py decision-review .warp/examples/decision-review-example.yaml returns rc 0.

scripts/selftest.py WARP-1106 block: 'the shipped decision-review example validates and binds via check_decision_review' (V.check_decision_review == 0), 'the shipped example names the example decision (DEC-0000) and carries no decision block' (a review informs, never decides), and the AC2 positive control 'a well-formed warp.decision_review/v1 review validates' (_dr_errs(GOOD_REVIEW) == 0).

validate_review in .warp/decision_review.py, invoked from validate.py check_decision_review, structurally checks a review the way decision.py checks a record and fails closed by name on: a wrong schema id, a missing/empty required field (id, decision, reviewer, recommendation), a non-integer version or decision_version, an out-of-vocabulary disposition or problem-class/dead-end/assumption verdict, an option_challenge or assumption_challenge lacking its finding, an empty option_challenges or assumption_challenges list, a duplicate option/assumption reference, a review that smuggles a decision (chosen, decided_by, decided_at), and a file outside the parser subset. Reuses validate.parse_yamlish (no second parser) and validate.fail (no import cycle).

scripts/selftest.py WARP-1106 AC2 negatives each refuse (>0): wrong schema, missing recommendation, non-integer version, non-integer decision_version, bad disposition, bad problem-class verdict, bad dead_end verdict, bad assumption verdict, option_challenge lacking its finding, empty option_challenges list, duplicate option_challenge, smuggled chosen option, smuggled decider; the positive control validates clean (0).

bind_review in .warp/decision_review.py pairs a review to the decision it reviews and fails closed when the record is malformed or absent (referenced but absent), when decision_version does not match the record's version (a stale review does not vouch for the current framing), and when the option_challenges or assumption_challenges do not COVER every option and assumption the decision declares, or reference one the decision does not declare. resolve_decision reads each record through the injected decision.load_record and matches on schema warp.decision/v1 and id, so a review-shaped file is never mistaken for a decision.

scripts/selftest.py WARP-1106 AC3: the well-formed review binds clean to its decision (0); an absent/malformed decision refuses (>0); a version mismatch refuses; an uncovered option refuses (partial attack); an option the decision does not declare refuses (referenced but absent); an uncovered assumption refuses. Plus the integrated positive: the shipped example binds to the shipped example decision via check_decision_review.

The fresh-context adversarial reviewer is a DELEGATED seam that FAILS LOUD, mirroring the executor's LiveLoop.review and the dispatcher's LiveReviewer. AdversarialReviewer.review(decision, context) is the seam; the reference LiveAdversarialReviewer is wired to nothing and RAISES DecisionReviewError, refusing to fabricate a review. No review's findings, disposition, or recommendation are synthesized in code: decision_review.py validates and binds an artifact a real fresh context produced, and an adopting runtime must inject a reviewer that dispatches a genuinely fresh context over the proposed decision.

scripts/selftest.py WARP-1106 AC4: 'the reference adversarial reviewer FAILS LOUD (refuses to fabricate a review)' (LiveAdversarialReviewer().review raises DecisionReviewError); 'DecisionReviewError is a ValueError (raised by name)'; and 'an injected reviewer is the only path an attack enters (the seam, not fabrication)' (a fake AdversarialReviewer subclass returns the attack, proving the seam is the sole entry point).

decided_requires_review over the decision records refuses a record whose status is decided unless it carries at least the number of bound, valid adversarial reviews its risk tier requires, read from .warp/policy.yaml risk_tiers (the single source of truth): irreversible maps to critical (two independent reviews, D5), standard needs one. A review counts only when it validates structurally AND binds (resolves, version matches, full coverage) with zero errors, so a malformed or partial review cannot satisfy the gate. Adoption safe: with no .warp/decisions/ and no .warp/decision_reviews/ directory the whole gate stands down (a repository with no decision records is byte-identically unaffected); the moment a decided record exists the gate fails closed. This repository carries no real decision records, so run_all's check_decision_reviews stands down here; the teeth are proven over temporary trees.

scripts/selftest.py WARP-1106 AC5 over a temporary tree (this repository's real policy.yaml copied in so risk_tiers is read): no .warp/decisions/ directory stands the gate down (0); a decided record with ZERO bound reviews is refused (>0); with one bound review passes (0); a decided CRITICAL/irreversible record with ONE review is refused (needs two, D5); with TWO bound reviews passes; a review bound to a stale decision_version does not satisfy the gate; a DRAFT (un-decided) decision needs no review (the gate does not bite before a human decides).

TEETH (anti-vacuity C1): over the shipped decision-review-example.yaml, stripping an option_challenge's finding and removing the recommendation each turn the check RED, reverting byte-identical; over a temporary tree, deleting the sole bound review of a decided record turns decided_requires_review RED. .warp/decision_review.py ships in the engine and is byte-identical across root, plugin/templates, and all 6 packs (drift empty), .warp/validate.py's edit and the capabilities.yaml entry (adversarial_decision_review, mechanical) are re-synced likewise (template sync and pack drift pass), and the init scaffold lays .warp/decision_review.py beside .warp/decision.py. required_reviews_for reads policy.yaml risk_tiers (standard=1, critical=2, high=1), defaulting to one (never zero) when absent. The delegated reviewer is honestly labeled a delegated seam that fails loud (NG5). No protected path is touched: the gate lives in the non-protected engine (decision_review.py, validate.py) and READS policy.yaml without editing it.

scripts/selftest.py WARP-1106 TEETH: stripping an option_challenge finding from the real example turns the check RED; removing the recommendation turns it RED; the unmutated real example validates and binds (positive control); a decided record with its sole bound review passes and DELETING that review turns the gate RED; decision_review.py and validate.py byte-identical root vs plugin/templates; the adversarial_decision_review capability declared mechanical; the init scaffold required_substrate includes .warp/decision_review.py.
